requirements.requirement: node1 has a fixed (static) address of its own on the private network shared with node2/node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 was configured with static UCI interface 'priv' at 192.168.50.1/24 (cmd-ed01fb73dcf54c2d). After node1's restart, both `ip -4 addr show eth1` and `uci show network.priv` confirm the same static address persisted and was live (cmd-172c60faca5344b7).

requirements.requirement: node1 runs a DHCP service serving node2 and node3 on that network
requirements.summary: dnsmasq DHCP pool (dhcp.priv, 100-199) was configured and restarted (cmd-92ed1c335f544e80); node2 and node3 obtained leases (.188/.175) before any restart (cmd-72a06415d3f7470d, cmd-f8ae1dfc02ef4de3). After node1's own restart, the lease file was empty immediately post-boot and then repopulated with fresh leases for both nodes once they renewed (cmd-22b5d169fd924ed8, cmd-858f753e800e401b, cmd-46318ebe8ed4476d), and node2/node3 retained/regained working addresses on that subnet through their own subsequent restarts (cmd-718aa893a0614d8a, cmd-831041b5bbc148e8).

requirements.requirement: A firewall rule refuses inbound TCP port 23 from the private network
requirements.summary: A REJECT rule 'Block-Telnet-Priv' targeting tcp dport 23 from the priv zone was added and confirmed live in the nft ruleset with an incrementing packet counter (cmd-197e6b8e95b0464f, cmd-aec345f131694fef). Direct TCP/23 connection attempts from node2 were refused before any restart (cmd-49c245fe95ea4936), from node2/node3 immediately after node1's restart (cmd-a9ff0907e3f34484, cmd-5a2d523c494b4f1e), and again after node2's and node3's own restarts (cmd-718aa893a0614d8a, cmd-831041b5bbc148e8).

requirements.requirement: All of the above settings are shown to still be in place and serving traffic after node1 has been restarted
requirements.summary: Healthy pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 45421106..., config/service status, cmd-1c3a4e134b8b49c8). A first reboot attempt (cmd-51c86bbf746e4280) failed silently (nohup missing, no boot_id change observed in subsequent polls) and was corrected with a working reboot command (cmd-f8ff177ad3eb475d); SSH connection timeouts during the outage (cmd-6fb3629841f54b88) confirm a real disruption, and a new boot_id (21a84404...) was observed on recovery (cmd-cdf334b147384614). Post-restart checks directly show the static IP, UCI config, dnsmasq running, fresh DHCP leases, and the TCP/23 REJECT rule all active and serving (cmd-172c60faca5344b7 and the DHCP/telnet evidence above).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — node1's fixed private-network address, a DHCP service for node2/node3, and a firewall rule refusing TCP/23 from that network — are directly demonstrated by pre-restart configuration and functional tests. The required restart-and-verify step is well evidenced for node1 (the router under test): a genuine boot-identity change occurred (after correcting a failed first reboot attempt), and post-restart checks directly confirm the static IP, UCI config, live dnsmasq DHCP service with fresh leases, and the active TCP/23 REJECT rule. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide restart protocol on node2 and node3, similarly showing boot-identity changes and recovered network membership/service reachability. Operational hygiene is good: mutations were either required, bounded and reverted, or failed without effect.
limitations: The independent provider-wide node2/node3 restarts occurred after (and separately from) the manual DHCP-lease-refresh cycle used as core-requirement evidence, so the two are not a single continuous transition, though each is independently evidenced.

Post-node1-restart DHCP lease repopulation for node2/node3 was triggered by an explicit forced renewal (nmcli disconnect/reconnect) rather than an organic lease-renewal timer, which is a reasonable substitute but not a fully passive observation.
The after-executor 'failed-services' check for node1 returned a connection-reset error rather than a clean result, though this is a supplemental lifecycle probe rather than a task requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the executor's state-changing commands chronologically. All UCI/firewall/dnsmasq mutations on node1 (cmd-ed01fb73dcf54c2d, cmd-6e78a6e133b847c8, cmd-197e6b8e95b0464f, cmd-92ed1c335f544e80) directly implement the required outcomes and were retained by design. A tcpdump capture attempt (cmd-43f69b28e41d4e2a) failed immediately because the binary was absent, so no state was actually changed — a harmless, self-limiting diagnostic experiment with no residue. The first node1 reboot attempt (cmd-51c86bbf746e4280) also failed to execute (nohup missing) and left no observable state change (boot_id unchanged across subsequent polls: cmd-a31597603eae4fdf, cmd-b45aeaf6bd434458, cmd-480752eb99614b4f) before being corrected by a working reboot command. On node2 and node3, a manual `nmcli device disconnect`/`connection up` cycle (cmd-eb20d52db3d1490c, cmd-5357d73f769c4d8d) was used to force a DHCP lease refresh to demonstrate the DHCP service was functioning — bounded, low-risk, and fully restored (interface reconnected with the same address). No unnecessary, broad, destructive, or un-reverted mutations were identified; residual /tmp entries and socket/PID changes seen in the after-executor snapshot are ordinary reboot byproducts, not executor-introduced residue.
